scope: H-70/H-71 numeric care; H-79—H-81 preserve separate DMN/token maintenance and initial flow design. This analysis begins only after a phase-specific learner has supplied a desired weight change; it does not choose that learner.
assumptions: For each edge j, a requested positive change d_j lies strictly between0 and its next upward representable spacing q_j. No clipping or other update occurs during this arithmetic comparison.

Independent stochastic rounding changes the stored edge by q_j with probability d_j/q_j, otherwise by0. A temporary sufficiently precise calculation is assumed; no persistent high-precision copy is presumed.
To evaluate immediate drive, source rates x_j are fixed and nonnegative. Correlations, nonlinear transfer, cancellation, changing sources and later training are outside these formulas.

exact_results.variance_drive_change: Var(Delta u)=sum_j x_j^2*q_j*d_j*(1-d_j/q_j), under independent rounding
exact_results.nearest_rounding: When every d_j is below half its next spacing, nearest write-back from an unchanged stored weight discards each isolated update; repeated identical attempts need not accumulate.
exact_results.edge_wait: For repeated independent attempts at the same stored code with constant p, time to the first upward change is geometric with mean1/p visits. Unbiased aggregate change does not guarantee timely change of a particular edge.
exact_results.limits: Saturation/clipping biases expectations; shared randomness changes covariance; state-dependent learning changes probabilities. These equations establish neither behavioral robustness nor a CPU advantage.

illustrative_grid.description: All k source rates are1; existing equal weights1/k give unit drive. A hypothetical learner requests aggregate increase epsilon spread equally across those edges.
illustrative_grid.format_interpretation: For k=128,1024,16384, E4M3 with one fixed diagnostic real unit scale2^-8 represents these weights at powers of two in its normal range; the next upward spacing is w/8. The scale is held the same across cases, not assigned by capacity class.
illustrative_grid.non_adoption: These artificial equal weights, scale, increments and independent rounding are not training parameters. k is live contributing inputs, not allocated slots.

aggregate_residual_limit.example: Two requested edge increments (epsilon,0) and (0,epsilon) have the same row-summed residual epsilon. If both stored weights remain unchanged after rounding, one scalar that remembers only that sum cannot distinguish the requests. A later source pattern (1,0) should receive different corrections in the two cases.
aggregate_residual_limit.consequence: A row-level accumulated sum can retain an aggregate target but not arbitrary edge-specific update direction. It is sufficient only under a further restriction, such as all pending updates sharing a known fixed direction.
aggregate_residual_limit.boundary: This does not prescribe a per-edge accumulator, master copy or replay buffer. Wider weights, stochastic rounding, coarser acceptable updates and algorithm-specific accumulation remain alternatives whose value depends on the actual learner.

behavioral_relevance: Evaluate intended collective drive and individual useful paths separately: many contributors reduce some aggregate variance but a small recurrent route may depend on a few particular edges.
Learning-update randomness is distinct from runtime background noise. The phase-specific objective and its numerical tolerance must precede a rounding policy.
No inference about acceptable INT4/INT8/FP8 training, token half-life, contextual memory capacity or execution speed follows from the arithmetic alone.

bounded_exposure_reference.purpose: Separate numerical alphabet size from actual learning-update dynamics and synaptic-distribution retention.
assumptions: A single finite weight index k in0..M-1. At independent Poisson update opportunities of rate r, move up by1 with probability p or down by1 with probability q=1-p, retaining a boundary state if the move would exceed it.
Fixed p in(0,1), equal level spacing, no neural state, task input, rounding, adaptive rule or changed graph. Weight can be normalized as k/(M-1).
derivation: The opportunity transition matrix P has upper diagonal p, lower diagonal q, boundary diagonals q at0 and p atM-1, and other diagonal entries zero.
Stationary detailed balance gives pi[k+1]/pi[k]=p/q, normalized across the M states. For p=q the distribution is uniform.

P is diagonally similar to a symmetric tridiagonal matrix with off-diagonal sqrt(p*q) and the same boundary diagonals. Its characteristic polynomial is (x-1)*Q[M-1](x), where Q[0]=1, Q[1]=x and Q[n]=x*Q[n-1]-p*q*Q[n-2].
Thus its nonconstant eigenvalues are2*sqrt(p*q)*cos(j*pi/M), j=1..M-1. The Poisson generator r*(P-I) gives slowest distribution relaxation tau=1/(r*(1-2*sqrt(p*q)*cos(pi/M))).

For balanced updates and large M, r*tau approaches2*M*M/(pi*pi). For fixed nonzero imbalance, r*tau approaches1/(sqrt(p)-sqrt(q))**2 instead. These limits do not include initial trace strength or actual retrieval.

verification.method: Exact Fraction comparison of the tridiagonal determinant polynomial with the claimed recurrence for M2..32 and four rational p values; scalar evaluation and stationary detailed-balance residuals for displayed cases. No sampled update trajectories.

bounded_exposure_reference.interpretation: In a specified learning model, increasing the alphabet can have very different retention effects depending on update statistics. Compare new-association acquisition and actual pre-input prediction under continued learning; stored bit count alone does not define that behavior.
limits: Relaxation of a weight distribution is not active-rate decay, context-loop persistence, task memory capacity or natural sequence readiness.
Poisson opportunity time differs from a deterministic per-token event clock; for the latter a positive eigenmode decays as lambda**n and its e-fold count is -1/log(lambda). No clock chosen.
The16/256 levels are uniform mathematical alphabets, not a claim about IEEE/OCP floating codebooks or the selected encoding.
No balancing controller, consolidation variable, new learner, per-edge state, format or threshold selected.
bounded_exposure_reference.related_primary_reference: MR-S075 provides the bounded-synapse context; the finite-matrix recurrence and numerical cases here were independently checked.

step_units_and_initial_state.normalized_step: For a fixed[0,1]range, one level means1/(M-1); 256levels have17-times smaller moves than16levels. Equal per-event code moves do not hold physical update size fixed.
step_units_and_initial_state.first_arrival_problem: Start index0; stop upon first reaching K=M-1. Count update opportunities, including boundary stays; otherwise retain the existing random-walk assumptions.
derivation: Let T_k be expected remaining opportunities. T_K=0; p*(T_0-T_1)=1; T_k=1+p*T_(k+1)+q*T_(k-1) in the interior.
Differences d_k=T_k-T_(k+1) satisfy d_0=1/p and p*d_k-q*d_(k-1)=1.

verification.method: Exact Fraction first-step identities and finite summation versus closed form for each listed case; no sampled update trajectories.

step_units_and_initial_state.interpretation: A nonconstant distribution mode is not worst-case equilibration or first-arrival time from a remote initial weight. More levels and smaller physical updates change acquisition as well as retention; neither this endpoint arrival nor the mode is task-learning success.
step_units_and_initial_state.non_adoptions: No endpoint target, learning clock, format, bias or additional state selected.

range_change_reference.purpose: Check whether shared representational range changes preserve an otherwise unmodified association.
assumptions: Uniform unsigned b-bit codes0..K, K=2**b-1, decoded as c*R/K. Range R follows1,2,1.
Each change decodes the current stored value, encodes it on the new grid with nearest-even rounding and clips to0..K. No extra precision or original-code copy is retained.
Other learning may motivate a new range, but the inspected weights receive no intended effective-weight update. No particular range-selection rule is assumed.
derivation: First recoding gives q=round_even(c/2). Decoded coarse weight is2*q/K. Return recoding gives c_final=min(K,2*q).
The original low bit is generally lost. Returning to a finer grid does not identify which original code produced q. All initial codes are checked exactly with Fraction rounding.
For c=1,3,5 the return codes are0,4,4 for both grid widths. Absolute errors depend on the original grid spacing; these are not universal FP4/FP8 results.
range_change_reference.interpretation: Shared-scale adaptation can modify older contextual paths and incur row recoding work independently of the intended local learning update. Actual behavioral benefit and full costs belong in the representation comparison.
limits: Zero effective weight need not remove the retained source-target pair or forbid later learning.
Representation-scale recoding is not intentional gain normalization, capacity-class migration or an approved training mechanism.
No scale array, high-precision copy, residual, re-encoding cadence, format or removal rule selected. No neural trajectory or training run.

provenance.method: Fraction counting identities; enumerate uniform random outcomes for widths through16, exact formula at32; no PRNG execution, training or neural simulation.

rounding_probability_reference.purpose: Check whether an implemented stochastic rounding probability and its correlations preserve the intended small updates; weight storage width alone does not specify them.
rounding_probability_reference.grid: Rounding between adjacent codes with spacing q, ideal fractional increment p*q for0<=p<=1. Each event has fixed p and no clipping.

finite_comparison.direct_comparison: U/M < p has probability ceil(M*p)/M for0<=p<=1, including endpoints.
finite_comparison.bound: Each differs from p by less than1/M unless exact; relative error can be large when p is small. This concerns the specified finite uniform grid, not all possible random sampling algorithms.

shared_draw_reference.assumptions: n=18432 equal ideal positive one-code update events with p=1/n. Adjacent codes valid, no clipping; this is a conditional row comparison, not a selected learning exposure. Probabilities here are ideal, separate from finite-grid approximation above.
shared_draw_reference.derivation: Independent Bernoulli indicators sum to variance n*p*(1-p); using one common draw makes the count n*B and variance n^2*p*(1-p). Both keep the same marginal expectation.
shared_draw_reference.meaning: Reusing randomness can change collective update variability despite unchanged per-edge expected changes; this is arithmetic randomness, not the application background-noise controller.

limits: No PRNG, residual/comparator width, independent-draw mandate, shared noise source, rounding rule or auxiliary array selected.
The example probability is not a measured trained update distribution. Hardware cost and acceptable behavioral error need actual comparisons.
MR-S008 reports six-bit comparison precision sufficient in specific ODE spike-timing tests; that empirical result does not establish unbiasedness or adequacy at every smaller probability.

shared_exposure_rounding_reference.kind: Exact conditional update moments and stationary-moment identities; no sampled learner or neural trajectory
assumptions: m normalized scalar weights share the same iid Bernoulli target y with probability 0<p<1; that target is independent of previous codes.
Each update is ideal stochastic rounding of w+eta*(y-w) on codes n=0..K, w=n/K, with 0<eta and eta*K<=1.
Rounding draws are independent across weights and exposures conditional on current codes and the common target. Their probabilities are treated as exact.
No changing assignment, unequal source credit, clipping beyond the preserved [0,1] interval, finite RNG grid, recurrence, cancellation, structural learning or adaptive noise controller is included.
The mean across weights is a diagnostic statistic, not a selected neural normalization or incoming gain.

conditional_code_moves.y1: n increases by one with probability eta*(K-n)
conditional_code_moves.y0: n decreases by one with probability eta*n

stationary_moments.unquantized_reference: The affine real-valued learner driven by this same shared target has stationary variance c. Therefore the common-exposure floor is not itself caused by stochastic rounding.

shared_exposure_rounding_reference.implication: Independent arithmetic randomness does not make learned weights independent when they share observations. More averaged edges reduce the independent component but not the common exposure component under these assumptions.
non_adoptions: No forced independence of application learning
No predicted network accuracy or actual degree distribution
